items.title: New Research Tests Whether AI Models Know Their Own Thoughts | Quanta Magazine
items.summary: To test their hypothesis, the researchers repeated Lindsey’s experiment on large open-source language models. They gave extra attention to cases where models correctly flagged an injection but failed to name the injected concept. You might expect that in such cases the models would guess somewhat related concepts — say “shirts” or “shoes” when the injected concept was “denim.” Instead, the models would get it completely wrong. “Bizarrely, they say ‘apple’ all the time,” Lederman said.

items.title: Tencent Launches Hy4, Joining the Ranks of the World's Leading Open-Source AI Models - Tencent
items.summary:
November 4, 2026

Tencent today announced the release of Tencent Hy4, its latest-generation large language model, marking a significant leap in performance and capabilities that now ranks it among the world’s leading open-source AI models. Tencent Hy plans to release model weights and system cards in the coming days, reinforcing its commitment to responsible open-source AI development, with a focus on cybersecurity and biological safety.

items.title: Open-Source AI Models: 8 Best You Can Run Yourself (2026)
items.summary:
### 1. Qwen 3 (Alibaba): Best all-round family

Qwen 3 from Alibaba is the most versatile open-source AI model family available. It spans 7 sizes from 0.6B to 235B parameters, supports 119 languages, and the smaller models (up to 32B) are released under the Apache 2.0 license. According to the Hugging Face open-source leaderboard, Qwen 3 235B leads open-source models on reasoning and coding benchmarks. [...] ### 8. Codestral / Devstral (Mistral AI): Best open-source coding model

Codestral is Mistral’s dedicated coding model, specialized for code generation, completion, and debugging across multiple languages. Devstral is the smaller variant designed for local development workflows. Among open-source AI models for coding, this pair offers the best combination of quality and efficiency. [...] Open-source AI models (more precisely “open-weight” models) are AI systems whose neural network parameters are publicly downloadable. You can run them on your own computer, your own server, or your own cloud instance without connecting to anyone else’s API. No data leaves your machine. No per-query cost. No dependency on an external provider’s uptime, pricing changes, or terms of service.

items.title: 8 LLM Frameworks to Watch as Microsoft and OpenAI Reshape the Stack
items.summary:
The martech landscape has fundamentally shifted with the rise of AI. Large Language Models (LLMs) have allowed organizations to do more with data than just conduct an analysis or a calculation.

The arrival of AI has increased accessibility to open-source LLM architectures that can train data to solve real-world problems, such as conversational AI that craft natural language answers to queries and automation of devices and other software to complete complex tasks. [...] vLLM is an open-source inference and serving engine designed specifically for optimizing the serving of large language models for production deployments.  Inference is a term often used with LLM design. Inference is the process of using a trained model to generate predictions or outputs based on new input data.
